figures.finding: Barbados's Cultural Industries Development Act 2013 gives an approved audio-visual producer duty- and tax-free import of production equipment and studio materials, a 100% write-off of spending on producing or acquiring local films, and 150% deductions for training and for marketing an approved project; it sets no cash rebate.

value.law: Cultural Industries Development Act 2013 (proclaimed 1 February 2015 per GIS Barbados; not read)
value.imports: exempt from all duties and taxes
value.studio: capital set-off over 10 years, property transfer tax exemption, interest subsidies

figures.applies: Barbados; approved producers of audio-visual content (companies under the Companies Act) in an approved cultural project.

sources.said: the approved producer shall be exempt from the payment of all duties and taxes payable on such imports of equipment, machinery and materials … respect of local films, then in calculating the assessable income of the approved producer for an income year, there shall be a write-off of 100 per cent. … to 150 per cent of the expenditure incurred.

figures.finding: The National Cultural Foundation's Cultural Industries Development Fund gives Barbadian citizens and companies grants for cultural work including film production: a Technical Assistance Grant up to BBD 5,000, and Product Development and Project Execution Grants up to BBD 30,000 each, one grant a year per entrepreneur, approved by the NCF Board.

value.limit: one disbursement per 12 months and per project
value.eligibility: citizens of Barbados; companies whose principal shareholder is a citizen

figures.applies: Barbados; as the NCF page reads on 2026-11-01.

sources.said: Cultural Industries Development Fund is open to all citizens of Barbados and companies registered in Barbados whose principal shareholder or partner is a citizen of the island. … fashion, visual arts, film production, performing arts … (Up to $5,000) … (Up to $30,000) … Creative entrepreneurs are limited to one grant disbursement within a 12-month period and one disbursement per cultural project.
